environment.prompt: Which environment does this resource support?
environment.description: Production criticality changes availability, recovery, and change-safety guidance.

criticality.prompt: How critical is this resource to the business?
criticality.description: Criticality determines the acceptable blast radius and verification depth.

owner.prompt: Who owns the workload or data?
owner.description: Ownership is required before destructive or disruptive work can be considered safe.

data_classification.description: Data sensitivity controls encryption, exposure, retention, and audit requirements.

access_pattern.prompt: What access pattern should this resource support?
access_pattern.description: Expected readers, writers, protocols, and frequency affect the correct architecture.

retention.prompt: What retention or deletion requirement applies?
retention.description: Retention determines lifecycle, backup, archival, and deletion safeguards.

recovery.description: RTO and RPO determine redundancy, backup, and failover controls.

traffic.prompt: What traffic or utilization pattern is expected?
traffic.description: Steady, bursty, seasonal, and low-volume workloads need different scaling choices.

growth.prompt: How much growth should the design tolerate?
growth.description: Expected growth determines whether current capacity and topology will remain suitable.

consumers.prompt: Which systems consume or depend on this resource?
consumers.description: Known consumers improve dependency and blast-radius confidence.

exposure.prompt: Should this resource be internet reachable?
exposure.description: Intended exposure is required to distinguish a risk from a deliberate interface.

compliance.prompt: Does a regulated or contractual control set apply?
compliance.description: Compliance context can strengthen encryption, logging, and retention requirements.

account_foundation.summary: Identity, account governance, auditability, and operational visibility.

storage_and_protection.summary: Data protection, lifecycle, recovery, storage efficiency, and network placement.

compute_and_runtime.summary: Runtime security, capacity, availability, scaling, observability, and deployment safety.

data_platforms.summary: Data availability, performance, security, recovery, and cost-efficient capacity.

edge_and_integration.summary: Ingress, routing, authentication, asynchronous integration, and service protection.

iam.business_impact: Compromised or over-privileged identities can expose every workload reachable by the principal.
iam.safe_correction: Plan least-privilege changes per principal, identify active callers, and preserve a tested recovery path.
iam.verification: Re-read identity configuration and validate intended callers before retiring old access.

cloudtrail.business_impact: Missing or incomplete audit trails delay incident response and weaken forensic evidence.
cloudtrail.safe_correction: Preserve existing destinations and permissions while adding validated audit coverage.
cloudtrail.verification: Confirm delivery, validation, encryption, and alarm integration with fresh control-plane reads.

cloudwatch.business_impact: Insufficient retention hides operational evidence; unlimited retention can create avoidable cost.
cloudwatch.safe_correction: Choose retention from incident, legal, and operational requirements before changing it.
cloudwatch.verification: Re-read retention and confirm new events remain queryable.

s3.business_impact: Incorrect access, durability, or lifecycle settings can expose data, prevent recovery, or accumulate cost.
s3.safe_correction: Validate consumers and data requirements before changing policy, encryption, lifecycle, or retention.
s3.verification: Re-read bucket controls and test an approved access and recovery path.

efs.business_impact: Shared file-system changes can affect every mounted workload and its recovery posture.
efs.safe_correction: Identify mounts and backup recovery before migration, lifecycle, or throughput changes.
efs.verification: Confirm mounts remain healthy and recovery controls still meet requirements.

ec2.business_impact: Compute or network changes can interrupt traffic, lose unprotected data, or expand attack surface.
ec2.safe_correction: Map traffic, storage, image, and recovery dependencies before resize, detach, stop, or delete actions.
ec2.verification: Validate health, traffic, storage attachment, and monitoring after an approved change.

kms.business_impact: A key policy or lifecycle mistake can expose data or make dependent data permanently unavailable.
kms.safe_correction: Inventory consumers and preserve decrypt access before policy, rotation, disablement, or deletion changes.
kms.verification: Re-read key state and validate encryption and decryption through approved dependent services.

secrets-manager.business_impact: Stale or broadly accessible credentials can compromise every consumer and complicate incident recovery.
secrets-manager.safe_correction: Identify consumers and validate dual-credential or rollback behavior before enabling rotation.
secrets-manager.verification: Confirm rotation succeeds and consumers authenticate without exposing secret values.

lambda.business_impact: Runtime, permission, or concurrency changes can break event processing or amplify downstream failures.
lambda.safe_correction: Validate callers, retries, concurrency, and downstream capacity before changing runtime behavior.
lambda.verification: Confirm successful invocations, latency, errors, throttles, and downstream health.

ecs.business_impact: Task or service changes can cause failed deployments, privilege expansion, or traffic loss.
ecs.safe_correction: Use immutable revisions, deployment health checks, and rollback criteria before changing tasks.
ecs.verification: Confirm desired tasks are healthy, traffic is routed, and rollback remains available.

eks.business_impact: Cluster and workload changes can affect many services at once; unsafe capacity or rollout changes can disrupt production.
eks.safe_correction: Correlate cluster, nodes, workloads, disruption budgets, traffic, and capacity before proposing a change.
eks.verification: Confirm control-plane state, Ready capacity, workload availability, events, and service routing.

rds.business_impact: Database changes can cause data loss, connection failures, or prolonged downtime across dependent applications.
rds.safe_correction: Establish consumers, backups, restore evidence, failover needs, and maintenance windows first.
rds.verification: Validate connectivity, replication, backups, performance, and application health.

dynamodb.business_impact: Capacity, index, or lifecycle changes can throttle applications or remove data without a recovery path.
dynamodb.safe_correction: Validate traffic distribution, indexes, consumers, recovery, and growth before changing capacity or storage class.
dynamodb.verification: Confirm latency, throttles, capacity, streams, and recovery controls.

alb.business_impact: Ingress changes can expose services, reject clients, or stop traffic to every registered target.
alb.safe_correction: Validate client compatibility, certificates, listener rules, and target health before changing ingress.
alb.verification: Test TLS, routing, target health, logging, and expected client access.

api-gateway.business_impact: API authentication, routing, or throttling mistakes can expose data or make client traffic fail at scale.
api-gateway.safe_correction: Identify clients and integration contracts before changing authorization, stages, or request handling.
api-gateway.verification: Test authorized and denied requests, integration health, logs, latency, and throttles.

sns.business_impact: Policy or subscription changes can leak messages or silently interrupt downstream notifications.
sns.safe_correction: Confirm publishers, subscribers, retry behavior, and message sensitivity before policy changes.
sns.verification: Publish a safe test event and confirm intended deliveries and denied unauthorized access.

sqs.business_impact: Queue configuration changes can expose payloads, duplicate work, or strand messages for dependent consumers.
sqs.safe_correction: Validate consumers, processing duration, retries, and dead-letter handling before queue changes.
sqs.verification: Confirm send, receive, retry, and dead-letter behavior with non-sensitive test messages.
